study: Schmidt et al. 2020, New Teacher Center induction (SRI eval of i3 scale-up)
eval_evidence: SRI International conducted the independent evaluation of the New Teacher Center's i3 scale-up grant; report explicitly distinguishes SRI's findings from NTC positions.
developer_evidence: 'NTC did not provide mentoring to teachers directly, but rather trained mentors who then worked with their assigned [beginning teachers]'; NTC built district capacity rather than delivering PD itself.
cascade_evidence: Train-the-trainer: NTC trained induction mentors (with NTC tools/training), and those mentors coached the beginning teachers (>=1 extra hop).
counterfactual_evidence: Control teachers received their districts' business-as-usual induction/mentoring; report found NTC treatment mentoring 'was not substantially different in key respects from the mentoring received by control teachers' (contaminated/active comparison).
coaching_evidence: NTC model = intensive, instructionally focused coaching via regular coaching cycles; mentors expected to meet beginning teachers weekly or more for an hour-plus.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention targets teachers (induction coaching/mentoring); no direct student-facing dose added.
maturity_evidence: Comprehensive induction newly implemented in the 5 scale-up districts; targets first/second-year (brand-new) teachers, impacts measured during this first scale-up implementation; fidelity was below thresholds at all sites.
